Abstract: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. This motivates safety sufficiency: whether a predictive interface preserves and exposes the policy-decisive information required to distinguish actions that may be EXECUTED, require clarification through ASK, or should be BLOCKED. We introduce SafeWebWorld, a benchmark for evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains through action-conditioned futures, policy-decisive evidence, and policy-conditioned decisions. Under a controlled Security-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning protocol, evidence preservation can improve substantially while authorisation-sensitive decisions deteriorate. As we’re still in the early days of building applications with foundation models, it’s normal to make mistakes. This is a quick note with examples of some of the most common pitfalls that I’ve seen, both from public case studies and from my personal experience.

Because these pitfalls are common, if you’ve worked on any AI product, you’ve probably seen them before.

1. Use generative AI when you don't need generative AI

Every time there’s a new technology, I can hear the collective sigh of senior engineers everywhere: “Not everything is a nail.” Generative AI isn’t an exception — its seemingly limitless capabilities only exacerbate the tendency to use generative AI for everything.

I've been playing with one of the examples from the paper and I'm delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well!

I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere) - YouTube

Genius piece of OSINT by Colsto, who demonstrates how you can take almost imperceptible background noise of planes from a video soundtrack, figure out their Doppler curves, then cross reference them against ADS-B data to find the exact location of the video based on their speed, distance, and gaps between different flights.

Via Lobste.rs

### Features

* **api:** add GA methods for analytics, spend limits and RBAC
* **api:** add named beta types for unified metrics and RBAC delete responses
* **api:** add shared analytics order and increase request actor types
* **api:** add tool_use_limit_reached_error and compaction_limit_reached_error session error types
* **api:** add types for analytics group_by and spend limit period filters
* **api:** add user_profile_id to External Keys and Workspaces


### Bug Fixes

* **api:** make spend_limit nullable in the spend limit increase request approve response
* **api:** require always-sent analytics fields and drop the unused project product field
* **client:** let pydantic validate params types that accept omit


### Chores

* **ci:** remove unused build upload steps
* **docs:** clarify the Slack channel id description
* **docs:** clarify what disabling the Compliance API stops
* **docs:** clarify what the capability_access_all role action grants
* **docs:** link Dreams model fields to the supported models section
* **docs:** update example user ID in Admin API examples
* **internal:** add a section for each repository's own review rules
* **internal:** plainer wording in work

events.excerpt:
<details open>

Add nccl support for multi-node tensor parallelism (#28967)

* Add a backend interface for collectives across ranks running in separate processes, implement it in the CUDA backend using NCCL, and use it in the RPC server when available.

* Drop ggml_backend_comm_allreduce_rank_t and reuse ggml_backend_comm_allreduce_tensor for per-rank communicators

* reuse ggml_backend_cuda_comm_allreduce_nccl for per-rank communicators. Remove the helper function backend_comm_proc_address

* Change ggml_backend_comm_get_unique_id_t and ggml_backend_comm_init_rank_t to more generic multi-process backend communicator interfaces

* set maxCTAs in ncclConfig_t to 8 for dgx spark in ggml_backend_cuda_comm_init_rank

</details>

**Website:**
- <https://llama.app>

**Attestations:**
- <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/63316073>

**macOS/iOS:**
- [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b12079/llama-b12079-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz)
- macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) [DISABLED](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/23780)
- [macOS Intel (x64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b12079/llama
